Timestamp when this guest user identity record was created.

The value corresponds to the created_at column in todo_app_guestusers and is set by the system when the record is first inserted.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this guest user identity record was last updated.

The value corresponds to the updated_at column in todo_app_guestusers and is refreshed by the system on each successful modification of the record.

ITodoAppGuestUser.IUpdate.description:
Data Transfer Object for updating minimal identity information of a guest user in the todo_app_guestusers table.

This update DTO allows modifying only the mutable business fields of a guest user identity record: external_reference, display_name, and status. Immutable and system-managed fields such as id, created_at, and updated_at are excluded from the request body and are controlled exclusively by the backend.

All properties of this DTO are optional because it represents a partial update operation. Omitted properties indicate that the corresponding database columns in todo_app_guestusers must remain unchanged, while properties that are present in the payload explicitly request that the backend overwrite those columns with the provided values.

Typical callers are the owning guest user or privileged internal components that need to adjust human-readable labels or external linkage identifiers for a guest user identity. The backend uses the guestUserId path parameter and the authenticated guestUser context to determine which row to update and to enforce ownership and authorization constraints.

external_reference.description:
Optional external reference identifier associated with this guest user identity.

This value can be used to correlate the guest user with external systems, analytics identifiers, device IDs, or other tracking references. It is purely a business-level identifier and does not carry any authentication or authorization semantics.

In the context of this update DTO, this property is optional. If it is omitted from the request body, the existing `external_reference` value in the todo_app_guestusers row is left unchanged. If it is provided, the backend updates the corresponding column using the supplied value according to business rules (for example, treating an empty string as a request to clear the reference if allowed).

display_name.description:
Optional display name or nickname for the guest user.

This field is used to present a human-friendly label for the guest user in administrative tools, logs, or UIs that surface guest identities. It may be empty or omitted when the system does not require a nickname for guests.

Within this update DTO, the property is optional and follows partial-update semantics: omitting `display_name` means the current value stored in todo_app_guestusers remains unchanged, while including it instructs the backend to overwrite the column with the provided value, subject to any length or validation rules defined at the service layer.

status.description:
Lifecycle status string representing the current state of the guest user identity.

Typical values include business-level states such as "active", "archived", or "blocked" depending on the broader status vocabulary defined for guest users. The exact allowed values are governed by higher-level business rules and potentially by the todo_app_todo_statuses catalogue model.

As part of this partial update DTO, the `status` property is optional. If omitted, the lifecycle status of the guest user remains as-is; if present, the backend updates the `status` column in todo_app_guestusers to the new value, which may affect whether the identity is considered active for future operations.

ITodoAppGuestUserSession.IRequest.description:
Search, filtering, and pagination criteria for listing guest user session records belonging to a specific guest user from the todo_app_guestuser_sessions table.

This request DTO is used with the PATCH /todoApp/todoAdmin/guestUsers/{guestUserId}/sessions endpoint to retrieve a paginated list of session summaries for a single guest user. It contains optional filters such as time ranges, IP address, and initial navigation URL, as well as pagination and sorting parameters.

All sessions returned by the corresponding operation are implicitly scoped to the parent guest user via the guestUserId path parameter, so this DTO does not include any guest user identifiers. It focuses purely on query behaviour and never includes system-managed fields like id or foreign keys.

page.description:
1-based page index for paginated session results.

When provided, this selects which page of the result set to return. If omitted, the backend applies a sensible default, typically page 1. Values less than 1 should be rejected or normalized according to global pagination policy.

limit.description:
Maximum number of session records to return in a single page.

This value controls page size for the paginated results. The server may enforce an upper bound regardless of the client-supplied value to protect system performance and prevent excessively large responses.

order_by.description:
Field name to use for ordering the session results.

Common values include "created_at" to sort by session creation time or "expired_at" to sort by session end time. The exact allowed fields are validated by the backend to prevent arbitrary or unsafe ordering expressions.

order_direction.description:
Sort direction to apply when ordering session records.

Typical values are "asc" for ascending order and "desc" for descending order. If omitted, the backend applies its default sort direction, usually descending by creation time for recent-first listings.

created_from.description:
Lower bound of the creation timestamp range filter for sessions.

When provided, only sessions with created_at greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time value are included in the result set. This is useful for investigating sessions starting from a specific point in time.

created_to.description:
Upper bound of the creation timestamp range filter for sessions.

When provided, only sessions with created_at less than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time value are included in the result set. This can be combined with created_from to form a closed time window.

expired_from.description:
Lower bound of the expiration timestamp range filter for sessions.

When provided, only sessions with expired_at greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time value are returned. Sessions that have not yet expired (null expired_at) are handled according to service-specific filtering rules.

expired_to.description:
Upper bound of the expiration timestamp range filter for sessions.

When provided, only sessions with expired_at less than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time value are included in the results. This is useful for looking at sessions that ended within a specific period.

ip.description:
Optional filter on the client IP address recorded for the session.

Implementations may support exact match or partial prefix matching depending on business needs. This field helps administrators investigate sessions originating from specific IPs or ranges.

href.description:
Optional filter on the initial href URL recorded when the session was created.

This is typically the full URL of the page where the guest user started the session. Filtering by href allows administrators to focus on sessions that began on particular landing pages or flows.

referrer.description:
Optional filter on the referrer URL captured when the session started.

This value usually indicates the page or domain that led the user to the initial href. Filtering by referrer can help analyze traffic sources and behaviors in specific funnels or campaigns.

ITodoAppTodoUser.IRequest.description:
Search and filter request DTO for querying Todo user accounts from the `todo_app_todousers` table.

This schema represents the request body of the administrative PATCH search endpoint that lists todoUser accounts. It encapsulates filter conditions such as email matching, account status constraints, and date ranges on creation or last login, as well as pagination and sorting instructions.

The DTO is designed for use by `todoAdmin` actors operating an administrative console or support tooling. Regular end users never interact with this type directly; instead, they use dedicated self‑service profile endpoints. The fields are purely query parameters and do not map directly to stored columns via `x-autobe-prisma-schema`, so the backend is free to interpret and combine them into SQL or ORM queries over `todo_app_todousers`.

page.description:
Page index for paginated user search results.

This value indicates which logical page of results to retrieve, starting from 1 by convention unless the implementation specifies otherwise. It works together with `limit` to control which slice of the filtered user set is returned to the admin caller. When omitted, the backend should fall back to a sensible default, such as the first page.

limit.description:
Maximum number of Todo user records to return in a single page.

This property controls the page size for search results and directly influences the number of `ITodoAppTodouser.ISummary` items in the response `data` array. The backend enforces an upper bound defined by business policy to prevent excessively large result sets, capping any larger requested value to the configured maximum.

email.description:
Email filter used to find Todo users by their login address.

When provided, this field allows admins to search for accounts whose `email` column in `todo_app_todousers` matches the supplied value according to implementation rules, such as exact match or substring match. The email is the primary login identifier, so this filter is the most direct way to locate a specific user when the address is known.

status.description:
Optional account status filter applied to Todo users.

Typical values include lifecycle states such as `active`, `suspended`, or `closed` as described in the `status` column of the `todo_app_todousers` Prisma model. When set, the backend limits the search to users whose status matches the requested value. When omitted, users of all statuses are eligible unless the implementation imposes an implicit default filter.

created_from.description:
Lower bound of the creation timestamp range filter for Todo users.

When present, only accounts whose `created_at` column in `todo_app_todousers` is greater than or equal to this timestamp are included in the results. Admins use this field to focus on recently registered users or to analyse growth over specific periods.

created_to.description:
Upper bound of the creation timestamp range filter for Todo users.

This value complements `created_from` and restricts the search to accounts created at or before the specified moment. Together, the two properties define a closed or half‑open time window for analysing account registrations.

last_login_from.description:
Lower bound of the last login timestamp range filter for Todo users.

When set, this filter includes only accounts whose `last_login_at` column is greater than or equal to the given timestamp. It is useful for identifying recently active users, monitoring engagement, or excluding dormant accounts from the results.

last_login_to.description:
Upper bound of the last login timestamp range filter for Todo users.

Used together with `last_login_from`, this value allows admins to search for accounts whose last successful authentication occurred on or before a particular time, supporting investigations into historical activity or inactivity windows.

order_by.description:
Field name used to sort Todo user search results.

Common options include `created_at`, `last_login_at`, or `email`, which the backend maps to the corresponding columns in `todo_app_todousers`. When omitted, the default sort is typically `created_at` in descending order, returning the most recently created accounts first.

order_direction.description:
Sort direction applied to the `order_by` field.

Allowed conceptual values are `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. When not provided, the backend assumes a default direction, usually `desc`, to prioritise the most recent or highest values, such as latest registrations or logins.

ITodoAppGuestUserSession.description:
Guest user session entity representing a single tracked interaction context for a conceptual guest user.

Each record corresponds to one session row in the `todo_app_guestuser_sessions` Prisma model and captures operational telemetry such as IP address, entry URL, referrer, and lifecycle timestamps. It is used for audit, monitoring, and guest-to-registered upgrade flows rather than for day‑to‑day business features.

The session belongs to exactly one guest user in `todo_app_guestusers` via the internal `todo_app_guestuser_id` foreign key, but this foreign key is not exposed in this DTO. Instead, ownership is expressed through the `guestUserId` path parameter of the associated API operation, and the backend enforces that the session row’s foreign key matches the path value.

This DTO exposes only non‑credential, telemetry‑oriented data and is intended for privileged operational tooling associated with the `guestUser` actor category.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the guest user session.

This value corresponds to the primary key column `id` in the `todo_app_guestuser_sessions` Prisma model and uniquely identifies one session across the entire todoApp system. It is stable for the lifetime of the session row and is used as the `sessionId` path parameter in the corresponding GET detail endpoint.

ip.description:
IP address from which the guest user accessed the service during this session.

This field mirrors the non‑nullable `ip` column in the `todo_app_guestuser_sessions` model. It typically contains the client IP as observed by the backend at the time the session was created and is used for security audit, anomaly detection, and traffic analysis. The exact textual representation follows the storage format chosen at the database level (for example IPv4 or IPv6 in string form).

href.description:
Full URL that the guest user initially accessed when this session was established.

This value reflects the `href` column in `todo_app_guestuser_sessions` and records the entry point of the session, including protocol, host, path, and query string where applicable. Operators and diagnostic tools use it to understand which page or flow started the guest interaction and to reconstruct navigation paths during investigations.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL indicating where the guest user navigated from when the session started.

This field is backed by the `referrer` column in the `todo_app_guestuser_sessions` table. It usually corresponds to the `Referer` HTTP header or an equivalent navigation origin and helps analysts determine traffic sources, cross‑site flows, and potential attack vectors. The value is captured at session creation time and is not modified afterwards.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this guest user session was created.

The value comes from the non‑nullable `created_at` column in `todo_app_guestuser_sessions`. It marks the moment the backend first recorded the session and serves as the lower bound for analysing guest activity and calculating session age. It is expressed in a standard date‑time format compatible with ISO 8601 semantics.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when this guest user session expired or was invalidated, or null while active.

This property maps to the nullable `expired_at` column in the `todo_app_guestuser_sessions` Prisma model. When set, it indicates that the session is no longer considered active, either due to explicit logout, timeout, or administrative invalidation. When null, the session is treated as currently active or without a recorded expiry, depending on surrounding business rules.

ITodoAppTodoUser.IUpdate.description:
Administrative update DTO for modifying a todo user account.

This request body type is used by todoAdmin actors when calling the `PUT /todoApp/todoAdmin/todoUsers/{todoUserId}` endpoint to change mutable attributes of an existing todo user stored in `todo_app_todousers`.

It allows controlled updates to fields such as `email`, `display_name`, and `status` while preventing modification of system-managed or immutable data like the primary key, password hash, and audit timestamps. All properties are optional so that clients can perform partial updates by sending only the fields they intend to change.

email.description:
New email address for the todo user, if it needs to be changed.

This maps to the `email` column in `todo_app_todousers`, which is uniquely indexed. When supplied, the implementation must enforce that the new email does not conflict with any other existing todo user account.

If omitted, the existing email address remains unchanged.

display_name.description:
Updated human-readable display name for the todo user.

This property corresponds to the nullable `display_name` column in `todo_app_todousers`. When provided as a non-null string, it replaces the current display name. When explicitly set to null, any existing display name is cleared.

If the property is omitted, the display name is left unchanged.

status.description:
Updated lifecycle status for the todo user account.

This value is written to the `status` column of `todo_app_todousers`. Administrative clients can use it to transition accounts between business states such as "active", "suspended", or "closed" according to established account lifecycle policies.

If omitted, the user retains their current status. Implementations may enforce additional business rules, such as restricting illegal state transitions, at the service layer.

ITodoAppTodouserSession.description:
Authentication session record for a registered todo user in the todoApp service.

Represents a single login session associated with a todo user account from the `todo_app_todousers` table. Each record captures contextual information about when and where the session was created and when it expires. This type is used as the detailed administrative view returned from the GET `/todoApp/todoAdmin/todoUsers/{todoUserId}/sessions/{sessionId}` operation.

In addition to the core session fields, this DTO exposes a lightweight summary of the owning todo user account so that administrators can understand which user the session belongs to without performing an additional lookup.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authentication session record.

This value maps to the primary key of the `todo_app_todouser_sessions` table and uniquely distinguishes this session from any other session rows for any user.

ip.description:
IP address from which this session was initiated.

This value is captured from the inbound HTTP request at the moment the session is created and is stored in the non-nullable `ip` column of the `todo_app_todouser_sessions` table. It always contains a textual representation of either an IPv4 or IPv6 address and is guaranteed to be present for every persisted session record.

Administrators use this field for security auditing, fraud analysis, anomaly detection, and troubleshooting connectivity issues. Because it is mandatory at the database level, API consumers should treat it as a required, always-populated value in responses.

href.description:
Initial URL that the client accessed when the session was created.

This usually corresponds to the page or endpoint where the user initiated authentication for this session and helps administrators understand the entry point context of the session.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL from which the client navigated when the session started.

Used for security auditing and traffic analysis. It may be an empty path-like URL or a minimal string if the user navigated directly or if the referrer header was not present.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this session record was created in the system.

The value reflects the moment the login flow successfully established the session and inserted the corresponding row into `todo_app_todouser_sessions`.

oneOf.description: Timestamp when this session expired or was invalidated.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when the session was terminated, revoked, or naturally expired.

While the session remains active, this field is null. Once the session is no longer valid, it is set to the time at which the session became unusable for authentication purposes.

owner.description:
Owning todo user account for this authentication session.

This summary object provides minimal identifying information about the registered todo user from the `todo_app_todousers` table who owns this session. It allows administrative callers of `GET /todoApp/todoAdmin/todoUsers/{todoUserId}/sessions/{sessionId}` and related APIs to see which user the session belongs to without issuing an additional user lookup.

The summary follows the standard `.ISummary` pattern, ensuring there are no circular references while still giving sufficient context for monitoring and audit views.

ITodoAppTodouserSession.IRequest.description:

Used as the request body for the PATCH `/todoApp/todoAdmin/todoUsers/{todoUserId}/sessions` operation. ITodoAppTodoAdmin.description:
Administrative user account entity for todoAdmin actors within the Todo application.

Represents a privileged operator who can access and manage Todo and user data for support, monitoring, and policy enforcement. Each record corresponds directly to one row in the `todo_app_todoadmins` Prisma table and exposes only non-credential, non-secret fields to API consumers.

This DTO is intended for read operations such as fetching a specific admin account or returning the updated state after a modification. It may be used in both detail views and internal administrative tooling, while keeping all password hashes and other sensitive authentication material hidden from responses.

id.description:
Primary key identifier of the administrative account.

This UUID value uniquely identifies one row in the `todo_app_todoadmins` table and is used in path parameters such as `todoAdminId`.

Clients receive this value from read/list operations and must never attempt to guess or fabricate identifiers.

email.description:
Unique email address for this administrative account.

This value serves as the primary login identifier for todoAdmin actors and must be unique across all admin accounts due to the unique index on the `email` column in the `todo_app_todoadmins` Prisma model.

The email is also commonly shown in administrative UIs for quick identification and search.

display_name.description:
Optional human-friendly display name for this administrative user.

When present, this field provides a label suitable for dashboards, audit logs, and oversight tools instead of, or in addition to, the raw email address.

If null, clients should fall back to displaying the email or another identifier.

status.description:
Lifecycle status of the administrative account.

Typical business values include strings such as `"active"`, `"suspended"`, or `"closed"`, representing whether the admin can currently authenticate or perform actions.

Implementations should validate status changes against business rules, but this DTO exposes the current status as stored in the `status` column of `todo_app_todoadmins`.

last_login_at.description:
Timestamp of the last successful login for this admin account, if available.

When non-null, this ISO 8601 date-time string indicates when the admin most recently authenticated through the login subsystem.

If null, the admin has either never logged in or the system has not yet recorded a last-login timestamp.

created_at.description:
Creation timestamp of the administrative account record.

This date-time reflects when the row in `todo_app_todoadmins` was first inserted and is managed by the backend or database layer rather than by clients.

Clients may use this field to sort or filter admin accounts by age or onboarding date.

updated_at.description:
Last update timestamp of the administrative account record.

Whenever mutable fields such as `display_name` or `status` are changed, this date-time is updated to reflect the most recent modification.

Consumers can use this value for auditing, cache invalidation, or change tracking in administrative tools.

ITodoAppTodoAdmin.IRequest.description:
Search and filter request DTO for querying Todo administrator accounts.

This type is used by the list/search endpoint for the `todo_app_todoadmins` table to express pagination, sorting, and filter conditions when retrieving admin account summaries. It does not map directly to a Prisma model but controls how results are fetched from `todo_app_todoadmins`.

Typical use cases include operational dashboards where operators need to search by email or display name, filter by status, and page through large sets of administrative accounts.

page.description:
Page index for paginated admin account listings.

Represents the 1-based page number to retrieve from the result set. When omitted, implementations commonly default to the first page.

Clients should not send values less than 1; such values may be normalized to 1 or rejected during validation.

limit.description:
Maximum number of admin account records to return in a single page.

This controls the page size for search results and helps prevent overly large responses. Service implementations may enforce an upper bound even if larger values are provided.

Typical values range from 10 to 100 depending on UI needs and performance considerations.

search.description:
Optional free-text search term applied to administrator identifiers.

Backends usually apply this term to fields such as `email` and `display_name` in `todo_app_todoadmins` to find matching admin accounts.

When null or omitted, no free-text search filter is applied and all admins matching other filters are eligible for inclusion.

status.description:
Optional lifecycle status filter for admin accounts.

When provided, only admin records whose `status` column matches this value (for example, `"active"`, `"suspended"`, or `"closed"`) are returned.

If null or omitted, accounts of all statuses are considered unless further restricted by business rules.

order_by.description:
Optional name of the field used to sort admin search results.

Common sort fields include `"created_at"`, `"updated_at"`, `"last_login_at"`, or `"email"`, although the precise set of allowable values depends on backend implementation.

When null or omitted, a sensible default such as `"created_at"` descending may be applied by the service.

order_direction.description:
Optional sort direction for the result ordering.

Typical values are `"asc"` for ascending and `"desc"` for descending ordering when combined with `order_by`.

If null or omitted, the backend applies its default direction, often `"desc"` for time-based fields so that the most recent records appear first.

ITodoAppTodoAdmin.IUpdate.description:
Data transfer object for updating non-credential fields of an existing Todo administrator account.

This DTO maps to the `todo_app_todoadmins` Prisma model and is used by administrative management APIs to modify mutable profile and lifecycle attributes such as `display_name` and `status`. It deliberately excludes credential fields like `password_hash` and immutable identifiers like `id`, ensuring that password changes and account creation are handled only through dedicated authentication flows.

All properties are optional so that callers can perform partial updates. The service layer will merge provided values into the existing record, enforce the unique constraint on `email` when it is updated, and apply business validation rules for allowed status values and transitions. Timestamps such as `updated_at` are managed by the backend and must not be supplied by clients.

email.description:
Optional new email address for the administrative account.

When provided, this value becomes the primary login identifier for the admin and must remain unique across all rows of `todo_app_todoadmins`, matching the model's unique index on `email`. The server is responsible for validating email format and enforcing uniqueness; clients only supply the desired value.

If omitted, the existing email remains unchanged.

display_name.description:
Optional human-readable display name for the administrator.

This value is shown in dashboards, audit views, and other management interfaces to make admin identities easier to recognize than by email alone. When omitted, the display name is left unchanged; when provided as an empty string or null (if allowed by the business layer), it can be used to clear a previously set display name.

status.description:
Optional lifecycle status for the administrative account.

Typical values include business-defined states such as `active`, `suspended`, or `closed`, corresponding to how the platform treats the admin's ability to sign in and operate. The backend validates any supplied value against allowed states and may enforce additional rules on transitions—for example, preventing changes from `closed` back to `active` without special privileges.

When omitted, the admin's current status remains unchanged.

ITodoAppTodoAdminSession.IRequest.description:
Search and pagination criteria for listing Todo administrator sessions from the `todo_app_todoadmin_sessions` table.

This DTO is used as the request body for session index operations scoped to a particular admin, allowing clients to specify paging and basic ordering parameters when querying that admin's sessions. It does not carry the admin identifier itself, which is supplied as a path parameter, and it never includes any actor identity fields.

All properties are optional so that callers can rely on backend defaults for page size or index when they do not need fine-grained control. The server combines these criteria with the mandatory constraint that only sessions whose owner matches the admin in the URL path are returned.

page.description:
Zero-based index of the results page to retrieve.

When provided, this value selects which slice of the administrator's session list should be returned, with `0` conventionally representing the first page. Negative values are invalid and must be rejected by the backend.

If omitted, the service applies its default starting page, usually the first page.

limit.description:
Maximum number of session records to return in a single page.

This value controls the page size for the paginated session listing and allows clients to balance between fewer network round trips and payload size. The backend may enforce an upper bound to protect performance and can substitute a sensible default when the client does not supply this parameter.

If omitted, the default page size configured by the service is used.

orderBy.description:
Optional field name to use when ordering session results.

Typical values correspond to columns on the `todo_app_todoadmin_sessions` table such as `created_at` or `expired_at`, allowing clients to view the newest or oldest sessions first. The backend should validate this value against an allowlist to prevent arbitrary column usage.

If omitted, sessions are sorted according to the service's default ordering strategy, commonly descending by `created_at`.

orderDirection.description:
Optional sort direction for ordered session results.

Expected values are business-defined directions such as `asc` for ascending or `desc` for descending order. When combined with `orderBy`, this controls whether earlier or later sessions appear first in the paginated data.

If omitted, the service uses its default direction, usually descending to show the most recent sessions first.

ITodoAppTodoAdminSession.description:
Detailed session information for a specific todo administrator authentication session.

This DTO exposes non-sensitive metadata from the `todo_app_todoadmin_sessions` table so that privileged administrative tools can inspect when and from where an admin session was established. It is used as the response body for operations that retrieve a single administrator session record for security auditing and troubleshooting.

The type is read-only from the client perspective. Session creation, refresh, and invalidation flows are handled by dedicated authentication services. This schema intentionally omits any raw tokens, secrets, or credential material while still providing enough context to correlate administrative activity with individual sessions.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the admin session.

This value maps directly to the primary key of the `todo_app_todoadmin_sessions` table and uniquely distinguishes each authentication session for a todoAdmin actor.

Clients can use this identifier together with the owning admin identifier to request detailed session information for audit or troubleshooting purposes.

todoAdmin.description:
Administrative user who owns this session.

This is the transformed representation of the `todo_app_todoadmin_sessions.todo_app_todoadmin_id` foreign key, exposing the owning administrator as a lightweight summary object instead of a raw UUID.

Use this field to understand which todoAdmin account established the session when reviewing security audits or monitoring administrative activity.

ip.description:
IP address from which the administrative user accessed the service during this session.

The value is recorded at session creation time by the authentication layer and can be used for security analysis, anomaly detection, or incident investigation.

It is treated as connection metadata and does not participate in authentication decisions on its own.

href.description:
Full URL that the administrative user initially accessed when starting this session.

This field captures the entry point into the system at the moment of login or session establishment, such as the dashboard or a specific admin tool.

It provides contextual information that helps understand user navigation patterns at the time of authentication.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL indicating where the administrative user navigated from when the session started.

Typical values include previous pages in the same application, external links, or empty strings when no referrer was available.

The value is captured as part of the session context and can assist in tracing how administrators arrive at the management interface.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this administrative session was created.

The value is stored using the database server's notion of time and represents the exact moment when the session became active.

It is commonly used for ordering session records, determining session age, and correlating activity with audit entries.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when this administrative session expired or was invalidated.

When the value is null, the session is considered active from the perspective of the session store, although higher-level logic may still apply additional checks such as inactivity timeouts.

When populated, it indicates that the session is no longer valid for authentication, but the record is retained for historical audit and security analysis.

ITodoAppActorSession.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for querying authentication sessions across all actor types in the todoApp system.

This DTO is used as the request body when administrative tools need to retrieve a filtered, paginated list of session records spanning guest users, regular todo users, and todo administrators. It describes which subset of sessions to return and how results should be ordered and paginated.

All fields are optional, allowing callers to combine filters such as actor type, actor identifier, IP address, and time ranges for session creation. When no filters are provided, the implementation may either return a default recent window of sessions or apply system-configured constraints to avoid excessively broad queries.

page.description:
Page number to retrieve in the paginated result set.

The first page is 1. When omitted, the implementation should default to the first page or a system-configured value.

This value is used together with `limit` to compute the offset into the unified session query across all actor types.

limit.description:
Maximum number of session records to return in a single page.

Typical values are constrained by system configuration to protect performance. When omitted, a sensible default page size such as 20 or 50 sessions is applied by the server.

Administrators can adjust this value within allowed bounds to control how much data is returned per request.

actor_type.description:
Optional logical type of actor whose sessions should be included.

The allowed values are aligned with the actor type vocabulary used by `ITodoAppActorSession.actorType` and `ITodoAppActorSession.ISummary.actorType`:
- `"admin"` for todo administrator sessions (`todo_app_todoadmins` / `todo_app_todoadmin_sessions`).
- `"user"` for registered todo user sessions (`todo_app_todousers` / `todo_app_todouser_sessions`).
- `"guest"` for guest user sessions (`todo_app_guestusers` / `todo_app_guestuser_sessions`).

When omitted, sessions from all actor types may be included, subject to additional filters. This filter allows administrators to focus the query on a particular user category when investigating authentication behavior.

actor_id.description:
Optional identifier of a specific actor whose sessions should be returned.

For `"user"` actorType values this corresponds to `todo_app_todousers.id`; for `"admin"` it corresponds to `todo_app_todoadmins.id`; and for `"guest"` it corresponds to `todo_app_guestusers.id`.

When provided together with `actor_type`, it precisely scopes the query to sessions for a single identity. When provided alone, the implementation infers the appropriate table or performs a union-aware lookup.

ip.description:
Optional filter for the client IP address associated with sessions.

When specified, only sessions that were created from this IP address are considered. This is useful for investigating suspicious activity or tracing sessions back to a particular network origin.

The value should match the normalized format stored in the underlying session tables.

created_from.description:
Optional lower bound for the session creation timestamp.

When provided, only sessions with `created_at` greater than or equal to this value are returned.

This enables administrators to focus on recent or time-bounded windows during security investigations.

created_to.description:
Optional upper bound for the session creation timestamp.

When provided, only sessions with `created_at` less than or equal to this value are returned.

It is typically used together with `created_from` to define a time range for session search queries.

ITodoAppActorSession.description:
Represents a normalized view of a single authentication session across all todoApp actor types.

This DTO aggregates session information from the underlying Prisma models `todo_app_guestuser_sessions`, `todo_app_todouser_sessions`, and `todo_app_todoadmin_sessions`. It is used by administrative audit APIs to inspect how and when a specific guest user, todo user, or todo admin interacted with the service.

The structure focuses on security- and troubleshooting-related fields such as actor classification, owning actor identifier, connection context, and lifecycle timestamps, while intentionally omitting any credential or token data. It is strictly read-only and is never used to mutate session state.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the session record.

This value corresponds to the primary key `id` of a single row in one of the Prisma session tables: `todo_app_guestuser_sessions`, `todo_app_todouser_sessions`, or `todo_app_todoadmin_sessions`.

It is a UUID generated when the session is created and remains immutable for the lifetime of the record.

actorType.description:
Logical type of actor that owns this session.

The allowed values mirror the actor type discriminator used in `ITodoAppActorSession.ISummary.actorType`:
- `"admin"` for sessions belonging to todo administrators stored in `todo_app_todoadmins` / `todo_app_todoadmin_sessions`.
- `"user"` for sessions belonging to registered todo users stored in `todo_app_todousers` / `todo_app_todouser_sessions`.
- `"guest"` for sessions belonging to guest users stored in `todo_app_guestusers` / `todo_app_guestuser_sessions`.

Together with `actorId`, this field lets clients and backend logic consistently determine which actor table a given session refers to without additional mapping layers.

actorId.description:
Identifier of the actor record that owns this session.

For `"guest"` actorType values this references `todo_app_guestusers.id`. For `"user"` it references `todo_app_todousers.id`, and for `"admin"` it references `todo_app_todoadmins.id`.

The combination of `actorType` and `actorId` uniquely identifies the logical identity that is authenticated for this session.

ip.description:
IP address associated with the session at creation time.

This field mirrors the `ip` column from the relevant session table (`todo_app_guestuser_sessions`, `todo_app_todouser_sessions`, or `todo_app_todoadmin_sessions`). It records the remote IP address seen by the backend when the session was established and is used for security audits and anomaly detection.

The format is a plain string and may contain either IPv4 or IPv6 textual representations depending on deployment configuration.

href.description:
Full URL that the client was visiting when the session was established.

This corresponds to the `href` column in the session tables and typically contains the absolute URL of the page where login or initial access occurred. It helps administrators understand the entry point of the session in the todoApp UI.

The value is stored as a URI string without additional normalization guarantees beyond what the application layer provides.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL for the initial request that created the session.

This maps to the `referrer` column in the session tables. It usually indicates the previous page or external site from which the user arrived when starting this session.

The field is useful for tracing navigation flows and for security reviews when investigating suspicious entry points.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when this session record was created.

This is a direct mapping of the `created_at` column from the corresponding session table and represents the moment the authentication or tracking session started in the system.

The value is expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC and is used in chronological audits and reporting.

oneOf.description:
Concrete expiry or invalidation time for the session when present.

This value is copied from the `expired_at` column of the underlying session table. It marks when the session was explicitly expired, timed out, or otherwise invalidated by the system.

Administrators can compare `expiredAt` with `createdAt` to understand session duration and to identify long-lived or abruptly terminated sessions.

Indicates that the session has not yet been marked as expired.

When `expiredAt` is null, the underlying `expired_at` column in the session table is also null, meaning the session is still considered active or has not been formally closed in the database.

expiredAt.description:
Session expiration timestamp, if the session has been closed.

This field is derived from the `expired_at` column in the corresponding session table and is nullable. When non-null it represents the time at which the session expired or was invalidated.

When the value is null, the session is still considered active or has no recorded expiration in the database.

ITodoAppTodo.IRequest.description:
Filter, sorting, and pagination criteria for listing todos owned by the authenticated todo user.

This DTO is consumed by the `PATCH /todoApp/todoUser/todos` search endpoint and is interpreted against the `todo_app_todos` Prisma model. It allows clients to express constraints on todo status, creation and due date ranges, soft-deletion visibility, and free-text matching of fields such as the title.

In addition to business-level filters, the type encapsulates pagination and sort options so that queries can take advantage of indexes defined on `todo_user_id` combined with `created_at`, `todo_status_id`, and `due_date`. All results are implicitly scoped to the caller's `todo_user_id` from authentication context; no ownership identifiers are accepted in this structure.

page.description:
1-based page index to retrieve for the todo list.

This value determines which slice of the filtered result set is returned. It is interpreted together with `limit` to compute the offset for database queries.

If omitted, the backend applies a sensible default such as page 1.

limit.description:
Maximum number of todo summary records to return in a single page.

This parameter is used in conjunction with `page` to control pagination size and should be bounded by server-side maximums to protect performance.

If not provided, the service uses a default page size appropriate for the todoApp UI, for example 20 items per page.

items.description:
Status code value drawn from `todo_app_todo_statuses.code`.

Each element restricts todos to those whose `todo_status_id` joins to a status row with the given business-level `code`, such as "ACTIVE" or "COMPLETED".

statusCodes.description:
Optional list of status codes used to filter todos by business state.

The values correspond to the `code` column in `todo_app_todo_statuses` and are translated server-side into the appropriate foreign key filters on `todo_status_id`.

When omitted or empty, the query does not restrict results by status beyond any defaults enforced by the application.

titleKeyword.description:
Optional keyword used to perform a simple text search over todo titles.

This value is typically applied using a case-insensitive containment or LIKE filter on the `title` column in `todo_app_todos`. It allows users to quickly locate tasks by a fragment of their title without requiring full-text indexing.

When omitted or empty, no title-based filtering is applied.

oneOf.description:
Lower bound for todo creation time in the filtered result set.

Todos whose `created_at` is earlier than this timestamp are excluded from the response.

Indicates that no lower bound should be applied to creation time filtering.

When null, todos are not filtered by a minimum `created_at` value.

createdFrom.description:
Optional start of the creation date range filter applied to `created_at`.

When provided as a date-time value, only todos created at or after this time are included in the results. When null or omitted, the lower bound is not restricted.

oneOf.description:
Upper bound for todo creation time in the filtered result set.

Todos whose `created_at` is later than this timestamp are excluded from the response.

Indicates that no upper bound should be applied to creation time filtering.

When null, todos are not filtered by a maximum `created_at` value.

createdTo.description:
Optional end of the creation date range filter applied to `created_at`.

When provided as a date-time value, only todos created at or before this time are included. When null or omitted, the upper bound is not restricted.

oneOf.description:
Lower bound for the todo due date range.

Todos whose `due_date` is earlier than this timestamp are excluded from the result set.

Indicates that no lower bound should be applied to due date filtering.

When null, todos are not filtered by a minimum `due_date` value.

dueFrom.description:
Optional start of the due date range filter applied to `due_date`.

This is useful when listing todos that are due after a particular instant. When null or omitted, the query does not restrict by a minimum due date.

oneOf.description:
Upper bound for the todo due date range.

Todos whose `due_date` is later than this timestamp are excluded from the result set.

Indicates that no upper bound should be applied to due date filtering.

When null, todos are not filtered by a maximum `due_date` value.

dueTo.description:
Optional end of the due date range filter applied to `due_date`.

This is commonly used to list todos that are due before a certain date. When null or omitted, the query does not limit the maximum due date.

includeDeleted.description:
Flag indicating whether softly deleted todos should be included in the result set.

When true, the query includes records where `deleted_at` is not null as well as those that are active. When false or omitted, only records with `deleted_at` equal to null are returned, hiding logically deleted items from standard lists.

This flag is primarily intended for advanced clients or administrative tooling; typical end-user views will leave it set to false.

Name of the logical field used to sort the todo list.

Allowed values are logical field identifiers such as `createdAt`, `dueDate`, or `status`, which the backend maps to concrete indexed columns on `todo_app_todos` (for example, `created_at`, `due_date`, or `todo_status_id`).

When omitted, the service applies a default ordering, typically newest `createdAt` first. Additional sort keys, if introduced in the future, should be added to this enumeration to keep the schema and implementation aligned.

Allowed values are logical field identifiers such as `createdAt`, `dueDate`, or `status`, which the backend maps to concrete indexed columns on `todo_app_todos` (for example, `created_at`, `due_date`, or `todo_status_id`).

When omitted, the service applies a default ordering, typically newest `createdAt` first. Additional sort keys, if introduced in the future, should be added to this enumeration to keep the schema and implementation aligned.

Direction of the primary sort order applied to the todo list.

Supported values are `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. The value is applied in combination with `orderBy` to control list ordering.
