ITodoAppTodo.description:
Detailed Todo item entity for the todoApp service.

Represents a single actionable task owned by a specific todo user, mapped directly from the `todo_app_todos` Prisma model. This type is used in read operations where clients need the full detail of a Todo, including ownership, status, timing, and soft deletion metadata.

The schema exposes only business-facing and lifecycle fields; ownership is resolved via the authenticated todo user and the `todo_user_id` relation, while status is modeled as a reference to the normalized status catalogue in `todo_app_todo_statuses`. System-managed timestamps such as `created_at` and `updated_at` are included for audit and sorting purposes, while `completed_at` and `deleted_at` describe the completion and soft deletion lifecycle of each Todo.

id.description:
Primary key of the Todo item.

This value is generated as a UUID by the persistence layer when a new Todo is created and remains immutable for the lifetime of the record.

Clients receive this identifier in read responses and use it as the `todoId` path parameter when performing detail, update, completion, restore, or deletion operations.

title.description:
Short human-readable title of the Todo task.

The title summarizes the action or task the user wants to complete. It must contain at least one non-whitespace character and is typically constrained to a reasonable maximum length so that lists of todos remain easy to scan.

Clients usually present this field as the primary label for the Todo in list and detail views.

description.description:
Optional longer description of the Todo.

This field allows users to record additional details, notes, or context that complement the short `title`. It may be null when the user chooses not to provide extra information.

Implementations should respect server-defined maximum length constraints but otherwise treat the content as opaque free text.

due_date.description:
Optional due date and time for the Todo.

Represents the target moment by which the user intends to complete the task. The value, when present, is an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC or a clearly defined time zone.

When null, the Todo has no explicit deadline and can be treated as unscheduled or open-ended.

status.description:
Current business status of the Todo.

This object references a row in the `todo_app_todo_statuses` catalogue and describes whether the todo is active, completed, or in another configured state. It exposes stable machine-readable codes and human-friendly labels suitable for UI rendering.

The relation is read-only from the perspective of this DTO; state transitions are performed through dedicated operations such as complete or restore, or through status-aware update logic.

created_at.description:
Creation timestamp of the Todo.

Represents the instant when the todo record was first inserted into `todo_app_todos`. This value is set by the system and never changes afterward.

Clients can use this field for sorting, display of creation history, and audit-related features.

updated_at.description:
Last update timestamp of the Todo.

Updated automatically whenever mutable fields of the todo change, including title, description, due date, or status transitions.

Clients may use this field to detect stale data, show "last modified" information, or implement optimistic concurrency strategies.

completed_at.description:
Timestamp when the Todo entered a completed state.

When the todo is marked as completed via the completion operation, this field records the completion time. If the todo is later restored to an active state, the field is cleared and set back to null.

Downstream analytics and UI components can use this value to analyze completion patterns and render completion dates.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the Todo.

When this field is non-null, the todo is considered logically deleted and must be excluded from normal user-facing listings and detail views. The record remains in the database for lifecycle, retention, or administrative access.

Client code typically never sees records where `deleted_at` is non-null in standard endpoints, but administrative tools may surface them for audit or recovery flows.

ITodoAppTodoStatus.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a Todo status entry from `todo_app_todo_statuses` for list and reference usage.

This DTO provides the minimal but sufficient subset of fields needed to show available statuses, attach a status label to a todo, or render status filters, without exposing all internal lifecycle metadata.

It is intended for lightweight usage in list responses, dropdowns, and embedded references where full status management details are unnecessary.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the status entry.

This corresponds to `todo_app_todo_statuses.id` and is used as the primary reference when linking todos to their current status.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable status code for the Todo status.

This reflects `todo_app_todo_statuses.code`, using values such as `ACTIVE` or `COMPLETED` that remain stable over time and can be used safely in integrations and client-side logic.

label.description:
Human-readable label for the status value.

This corresponds to `todo_app_todo_statuses.label` and is typically displayed in user interfaces, for example as "Active" or "Completed" in status badges or select options.

is_default.description:
Indicates whether this status is configured as the default for new Todos.

This mirrors `todo_app_todo_statuses.is_default` and allows clients and admin tools to know which status will apply when none is explicitly chosen.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating whether this status is currently assignable to new or existing Todos.

This maps to `todo_app_todo_statuses.is_active` and distinguishes usable statuses from deprecated ones that remain only for historical references.

ITodoAppTodo.ICreate.description:
Request payload for creating a new Todo item in the todoApp service.

This DTO models the client-supplied fields that are allowed at creation time for a todo record backed by the `todo_app_todos` Prisma model. It exposes only business-level inputs such as title, optional description, and optional due date while omitting system-managed fields and ownership metadata.

Ownership is inferred from the authenticated todo user and injected server-side into `todo_user_id`. Status selection can either default to a configured initial status or accept an optional explicit status code depending on business rules; this DTO supports an optional `status_code` for that purpose without exposing foreign key identifiers directly. All timestamps, including `created_at`, `updated_at`, `completed_at`, and `deleted_at`, are managed by the backend and are not accepted from the client.

title.description:
Short title for the new Todo task.

Clients must provide a non-empty, human-readable summary of the task. The value should contain at least one non-whitespace character and respect maximum length constraints so that Todo lists stay readable.

This is the only strictly required business field for creating a todo and forms the primary label in most user interfaces.

description.description:
Optional detailed description for the new Todo.

Allows users to supply additional context, steps, or notes related to the task at creation time. When omitted or explicitly set to null, the todo will be created without extended descriptive text.

Servers may enforce maximum length limits but otherwise treat the content as free-form text.

due_date.description:
Optional due date and time for the new Todo.

If provided, this field records the target completion moment for the task as an ISO 8601 timestamp. When null or omitted, the todo has no explicit deadline and can be treated as unscheduled.

Validation should ensure that the value, when present, is a correctly formatted date-time string and may apply additional business rules, such as not allowing dates far in the past.

status_code.description:
Optional business status code to assign at creation.

When supplied, this value must correspond to the `code` of an active row in the `todo_app_todo_statuses` catalogue and determines the initial status of the todo (for example, `ACTIVE`). When omitted or null, the backend will apply its default status based on configuration and business rules.

This field allows clients to influence initial state without directly manipulating internal foreign key identifiers such as `todo_status_id`.

ITodoAppTodo.IUpdate.description:
Update payload for modifying mutable fields of an existing Todo item in the todoApp service.

This DTO maps to the `todo_app_todos` Prisma model and exposes only those columns that are allowed to change after the todo has been created. It is used by authenticated todoUser actors when calling the update endpoint for a specific todo identified by the path parameter `todoId`.

Ownership fields, primary keys, and system-managed lifecycle timestamps such as `id`, `todo_user_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `completed_at`, and `deleted_at` are excluded from the request body. The server is responsible for enforcing user ownership, updating timestamps, handling completion and deletion flows, and validating state transitions in conjunction with the `todo_app_todo_statuses` catalogue.

All properties in this DTO are optional to support partial updates; clients send only the fields they intend to change. Business validation still applies, so values like `title` must remain valid when provided, and status-related fields must respect configured status rules and lifecycle policies.

title.description:
Short text title describing the task.

This value updates the existing todo title stored in the `title` column of `todo_app_todos`. When provided, it must still satisfy the business rules for todo titles, including containing at least one non-whitespace character and not exceeding the maximum length used to keep lists readable.

If omitted from the request, the existing title is left unchanged.

description.description:
Longer free-form description of the todo task, or null to clear it.

This maps to the nullable `description` column in `todo_app_todos`. Clients may send a non-empty string to replace the current detailed content, an empty string when allowed by business rules, or explicit null to remove any previously stored description.

If this property is omitted, the description field in the database remains unchanged.

due_date.description:
Optional due date and time for the todo item, or null to remove it.

This corresponds to the nullable `due_date` column in `todo_app_todos` and should be provided as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or with an explicit offset. Providing a value updates the target completion time for the todo, while sending null clears any existing due date.

If omitted, the current due date stored in the record is preserved.

todo_status_id.description:
Identifier of the new status to apply to this todo, if changing its state.

This field maps to the non-nullable `todo_status_id` foreign key in `todo_app_todos`, which references the primary key of `todo_app_todo_statuses`. When supplied, the value must be a valid UUID corresponding to an active status row allowed for user updates.

If this property is omitted, the todo keeps its current status. The server enforces that any attempted transition complies with business rules, such as setting or clearing completion-related metadata when moving between active and completed states.

ITodoAppTodoAdminAudit.IRequest.description:
Search and filter parameters for listing administrative audit log entries for a specific todo item.

This DTO is used by todoAdmin actors with the PATCH `/todoApp/todoAdmin/todos/{todoId}/adminAudits` operation to query the `todo_app_todo_admin_audits` Prisma model. It carries pagination options and optional filters that narrow down the audit trail for the todo identified by the `todoId` path parameter.

The request never includes identity fields for the todo or the admin; those are derived from the path parameter and the authenticated admin context. Instead, it focuses on result-window control and field-based search criteria such as action codes, field names, and created_at ranges.

Implementations should validate pagination bounds and treat omitted filters as wildcards that do not restrict the result set.

page.description:
1-based page index indicating which slice of results to return.

This value controls the offset into the ordered audit record set for the requested todo. A value of 1 refers to the first page of results. Implementations should enforce a minimum of 1 and may cap the maximum supported page to protect performance.

If omitted, the server typically defaults to the first page.

limit.description:
Maximum number of audit records to return in a single page.

This property defines the page size used when scanning `todo_app_todo_admin_audits` for the specified todo. It should be a positive integer within service-defined bounds to avoid excessively large responses. Common values might range between 10 and 100.

When not provided, the backend applies a sensible default page size while still enforcing the global maximum.

action.description:
Optional filter for the audit action type code.

This value should match the `action` column in `todo_app_todo_admin_audits`, which stores short labels such as `update`, `delete`, `restore`, or `status_change`. When supplied, the result set is restricted to audit entries whose action field equals this value.

If null or omitted, no action-based filtering is applied and all action types are included.

field_name.description:
Optional filter for the specific field name affected by admin actions.

This filter corresponds to the nullable `field_name` column on `todo_app_todo_admin_audits`. When set to a non-null string, only audit records where the named field was targeted (for example `title` or `status`) are returned. It helps administrators focus on changes to particular attributes.

If null or omitted, the query does not filter by field and includes both field-specific and general audit entries.

admin_id.description:
Optional filter by administrative actor who performed the action.

This value is compared against the `todo_app_todoadmin_id` foreign key in `todo_app_todo_admin_audits`. Supplying a UUID restricts results to records created by that specific admin account, supporting operator-centric investigations.

When null or not provided, audit entries from all admins are considered.

created_from.description:
Start of the created_at date-time range for audit records to include.

This boundary is applied to the `created_at` column in `todo_app_todo_admin_audits`. When provided, only audit rows whose creation time is greater than or equal to this value are returned. It is typically used together with `created_to` to define a time window.

If null or omitted, there is no lower bound on the creation time filter.

created_to.description:
End of the created_at date-time range for audit records to include.

This property constrains the upper bound of the `created_at` column in `todo_app_todo_admin_audits`. When set, only records whose creation time is less than or equal to this timestamp are returned. Combining it with `created_from` creates a closed interval filter.

If null or missing, there is no upper bound on the creation time filter.

ITodoAppTodoAdminAudit.description:
Administrative audit record for a single change performed by a todo administrator on a specific todo item.

This DTO exposes the full append-only audit row from the `todo_app_todo_admin_audits` table, including the action label, optional field-level change information, a free-form reason, the creation timestamp, and rich context about the target todo and the acting administrator.

It is intended exclusively for administrative inspection scenarios, such as viewing a detailed audit entry in an admin console after selecting it from a list view. The referenced todo and admin entities are exposed as summary objects to provide complete context in a single response without creating circular references or forcing additional lookups.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the administrative audit record.

This corresponds directly to `todo_app_todo_admin_audits.id` and uniquely identifies a single audit event for a todo item.

action.description:
Short code or label that categorises the administrative action.

Typical values include labels such as `update`, `delete`, `restore`, or `status_change`, and are used for filtering and summarising audit activity in admin interfaces.

field_name.description:
Optional name of the specific field that was changed by this action.

When the action targets a particular attribute, such as `title` or `status`, this field contains that column name; it is `null` for actions that are not field-specific, such as full deletions or restores.

previous_value.description:
Optional textual representation of the previous value before the administrative change.

This is used to understand which value was overwritten. It is `null` for actions where a prior value is not applicable or not captured, such as initial creations or hard deletions.

new_value.description:
Optional textual representation of the new value after the administrative change.

This reflects the resulting state produced by the action. It is `null` for operations where no new value is applicable, such as deletions or rollbacks to an earlier state.

reason.description:
Optional free-form explanation provided by the administrator to justify the action.

This text can capture policy references, abuse-handling notes, or support-related context and is useful when reviewing historical changes or resolving disputes.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this administrative action was recorded.

The value corresponds to `todo_app_todo_admin_audits.created_at` and is used for chronological sorting and timeline reconstruction of todo changes by administrators.

todo.description:
Summary representation of the todo item affected by this administrative action.

This association replaces the raw foreign key `todo_app_todo_id` and exposes key fields of the todo (such as identifier, title, and status) so that administrators can understand which todo was changed without making additional API calls.

admin.description:
Summary representation of the administrative user who performed the action.

This association replaces the raw foreign key `todo_app_todoadmin_id` and exposes key identity and display fields for the administrator, enabling accountability and clear attribution of changes in audit views without requiring separate lookups.

ITodoAppSystemConfig.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a todoApp system configuration entry.

This DTO exposes only the essential identifying and descriptive fields needed to display or list configuration entries without revealing internal implementation details. It is optimized for lightweight read operations such as admin configuration overviews.

Each summary instance corresponds directly to a row in the `todo_app_system_configs` Prisma model and respects its field definitions and constraints.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the system configuration entry.

This value maps to the primary key `id` column in `todo_app_system_configs` and is used to reference or retrieve the full configuration record when necessary.

scope.description:
Logical namespace for this configuration entry, such as `todo`, `auth`, or `system`.

This value maps to the non-nullable `scope` column of `todo_app_system_configs` and is used to group and filter related configuration keys.

key.description:
Configuration key name within its scope, such as `deletion_model` or `soft_delete_retention_days`.

This field corresponds to the non-nullable `key` column and, together with `scope`, must be unique as enforced by the unique index on `(scope, key)`.

value.description:
Configuration value stored as text for this system configuration entry.

This property maps to the non-nullable `value` column in `todo_app_system_configs`. The consuming services are responsible for interpreting this text as a boolean, number, JSON, or other structured data according to the configuration semantics.

description.description:
Optional human-readable description that explains the purpose and allowed values of this configuration entry.

This property maps to the nullable `description` column and may be null when no extra explanation is provided.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating whether this configuration entry is currently active and should affect runtime behavior.

This property corresponds to the non-nullable `is_active` column. Inactive entries can remain in the database for audit or rollback but must be ignored by configuration loaders.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this configuration entry was created.

This field maps to the non-nullable `created_at` column and is expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this configuration entry was last updated.

This property is linked to the non-nullable `updated_at` column and is updated whenever the configuration entry changes.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this configuration entry.

This field mirrors the nullable `deleted_at` column of `todo_app_system_configs`. When non-null, the configuration entry is logically removed but preserved for historical and audit purposes.

ITodoAppTodoUser.ISummary.description:
Summary information about a registered todo user in the Todo application.

This DTO is optimized for list views and cross-entity references where a compact representation of a todo user is sufficient, such as ownership displays on todo items or admin user lists. It does not include sensitive fields like passwords, tokens, or internal flags.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the todo user.

This corresponds to the primary key of the `todo_app_todousers` table and is used throughout the system as the stable identifier for the user.

email.description:
Email address of the todo user.

Used as the primary login identifier and for notification delivery. This value is unique per user within the system.

display_name.description:
Human-friendly display name of the todo user.

Shown in user interfaces when referencing the user, such as in ownership labels for todo items or in administration consoles.

status.description:
High-level status flag representing whether the todo user account is active.

Typical values include logical states like `active` or `disabled`. This field is exposed so that list views and admin screens can quickly determine if an account is usable without loading full detail information.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the todo user account was created.

Stored in ISO 8601 date-time format in UTC. Used for audit, sorting, and display in administrative views.

ITodoAppTodouserSession.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a todoApp todouser session used when embedding session info into other DTOs or list views.

This representation is strictly aligned with the `todo_app_todouser_sessions` Prisma model and exposes only non-sensitive, high-level information about the session for display and auditing purposes. It does not contain any credential material, refresh tokens, or secret session identifiers.

In addition to intrinsic session fields, it now includes a lightweight summary of the owning todo user so that administrative and monitoring views can understand session ownership without issuing extra API calls.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the todo user session record.

This corresponds to the primary key of the `todo_app_todouser_sessions` table and is used to reference this session from administrative monitoring or audit payloads.

todoUser.description:
Summary information about the todo user who owns this session.

This replaces the raw foreign key `todo_app_todouser_id` in the response DTO and provides immediate context about the account associated with the session, including identity, status, and creation timestamp, without requiring a separate lookup.

ip.description:
IP address from which the todo user accessed the service during this session.

Captured at session creation time from the incoming request context and used for security monitoring, anomaly detection, and audit trail purposes. This value contains no secret token data but should still be handled as personal data under privacy regulations.

href.description:
Full URL that the todo user initially accessed when starting this session.

Represents the entry-point location in the client application at the moment the session was created. Useful for analyzing user flows, troubleshooting login issues, and building security or audit reports without exposing any authentication secrets.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL indicating where the todo user navigated from when the session started.

Typically populated from the HTTP `Referer` header at the time of session creation. This helps reconstruct navigation paths and investigate suspicious access patterns while remaining free of credential information.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this todo user session was created.

Stored in ISO 8601 date-time format in UTC. Used to order sessions chronologically and to understand when a particular authenticated interaction window started for the owning user.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when this session expired or was invalidated, or null while the session remains active.

When non-null, this value indicates that the session is no longer considered valid for authentication purposes. It supports security analytics, retrospective investigations, and implementation of manual or automatic session invalidation flows.

ITodoAppTodoAdmin.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a todoApp todoadmin account used in list views, embeddings, and audit payloads.

Contains only non-sensitive, high-level identification information about an administrator mapped directly from the `todo_app_todoadmins` Prisma model. This summary is intended for lightweight list responses and administrative tables where full detail is unnecessary.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the administrator account.

This value corresponds to the `id` primary key column of the `todo_app_todoadmins` table and is used to reference the admin in detail and update operations.

email.description:
Primary email address of the administrator, used for login and notifications.

This value is backed by the `email` column in `todo_app_todoadmins`, which is uniquely indexed to prevent duplicate administrator login identifiers.

display_name.description:
Human-readable name of the administrator used in UI and audit trails.

This property maps to the nullable `display_name` column of the `todo_app_todoadmins` table. When not set at the database level, clients may choose to fall back to the email address for display purposes.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of this administrative account.

This property is backed by the non-nullable `status` column in the `todo_app_todoadmins` table. Typical values include codes such as "active", "suspended", or "closed", which determine whether the account can authenticate and what operations it may perform.

List views and audit tools can use this field to highlight disabled or high-risk accounts and to filter administrators by their current operational state.

last_login_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent successful login for this administrator account.

This corresponds to the nullable `last_login_at` column on the `todo_app_todoadmins` table. It is expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC when present, and remains null if the administrator has never logged in.

Security and monitoring tools often rely on this value to detect stale accounts, unusual login gaps, or recent activity during incident investigations.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this administrative account was created.

This value comes from the non-nullable `created_at` column in the `todo_app_todoadmins` Prisma model and is managed by the backend or database. It provides a stable audit point for when the admin account was first registered.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this administrative account record was last updated.

This maps to the non-nullable `updated_at` column on `todo_app_todoadmins`. It is automatically maintained by the backend layer whenever mutable fields such as status or display name are changed, providing a reliable marker for the most recent configuration change to the account.

ITodoAppActorSession.ISummary.description:
Unified summary view of a session for any todoApp actor, including admin, registered user, or guest.

This abstraction allows monitoring tools and higher-level APIs to present session information without needing separate DTOs for each actor type.

Internally, it can be backed by `todo_app_todoadmin_sessions`, `todo_app_todouser_sessions`, or `todo_app_guestuser_sessions`, with an explicit actor type discriminator and a polymorphic actor summary reference.

id.description:
Unique identifier of this actor session.

For admin sessions this corresponds to `todo_app_todoadmin_sessions.id`, for user sessions to `todo_app_todouser_sessions.id`, and for guest sessions to `todo_app_guestuser_sessions.id`.

The identifier allows cross-actor monitoring tools to work with a single unified session reference.

oneOf.description:
Type of actor that owns this session.

`"admin"` indicates the session originates from a todo admin account stored in `todo_app_todoadmins`.

`"user"` indicates a registered todo user from `todo_app_todousers`.

`"guest"` represents a guest user identity from `todo_app_guestusers`.

This field allows clients to display key identity information for the session owner while keeping the unified session representation.

ip.description:
IP address from which the actor accessed the service during this session.

This is taken from `ip` in the underlying session table (admin, user, or guest) and is useful for security analysis, anomaly detection, and support investigation.

href.description:
Full URL that the actor initially accessed when the session was created.

Represents the entry point into the application for this session and is sourced from the relevant session table's `href` column.

This helps reconstruct common navigation flows and supports security review of suspicious access patterns.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL indicating where the actor navigated from when this session started.

Captured from the client request at the time the session was established and stored in the corresponding session table's `referrer` column.

Useful for understanding traffic sources and potential phishing or redirect scenarios.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this session was created.

Represents the moment a valid session record was inserted into the appropriate session table and is used as the primary indicator of session start time.

Clients and monitoring tools can sort by this value to review recent activity.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when this session expired or was explicitly invalidated.

When non-null, this indicates that the session is no longer active, due to logout, timeout, or administrative action. The value comes from the `expired_at` column of the corresponding session table.

A null value means the session is currently considered active according to backend policies.

ITodoAppTodoAdminSession.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a todo admin session used in list responses and as a reference from other administrative monitoring APIs.

This summary focuses on identifying information and key timestamps for a single administrative session without exposing low-level authentication details or sensitive security tokens.

It is typically used when browsing or auditing recent admin activity, correlating actions with the session context stored in the `todo_app_todoadmin_sessions` table.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the todo admin session.

This maps directly to `todo_app_todoadmin_sessions.id` and is used to reference a specific session in monitoring or administrative tools.

The value is generated by the system and is immutable for the lifetime of the session record.

todoAdmin.description:
Administrative user who owns this session.

This is a transformed reference for `todo_app_todoadmin_sessions.todo_app_todoadmin_id`, exposing the admin as a summary object rather than a raw foreign key.

Use this to understand which admin account established the session when reviewing audit logs or session lists.

ip.description:
IP address from which the administrative user accessed the service during this session.

Represents the remote address observed when the session was created and is useful for security review, anomaly detection, or support investigations.

The value is stored in `todo_app_todoadmin_sessions.ip` and is not editable by clients.

href.description:
Full URL that the administrative user initially accessed when starting this session.

This provides contextual information about where in the application the session originated, helping administrators understand entry points and navigation flows.

The value comes from `todo_app_todoadmin_sessions.href` and is typically captured from the client request at login time.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL indicating where the administrative user navigated from when the session started.

This field assists in reconstructing navigation paths into the application, which can be useful for traffic analysis and security audits.

It maps to `todo_app_todoadmin_sessions.referrer` and is recorded at session creation.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this administrative session was created.

Represents the exact moment the session became valid after a successful authentication event and is stored in `todo_app_todoadmin_sessions.created_at`.

Used for ordering sessions chronologically and for calculating session age.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when this administrative session expired or was invalidated.

When non-null, this maps to `todo_app_todoadmin_sessions.expired_at` and indicates that the session is no longer active due to logout, timeout, or administrative revocation.

Null means the session is currently considered active according to the backend's session lifecycle rules.

ITodoAppTodo.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a todo item in the todoApp service, optimized for list views and lightweight responses.

Provides essential identifying and status information for a single todo without heavy text fields or nested relations. Intended for use in endpoints that list many todos or embed todos inside other entities.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the todo item.

This value is generated by the system when the todo is created and is immutable for the lifetime of the record.

title.description:
Short title of the todo item.

Used as the primary human-readable label in lists and overviews. Typically a single line summary of what needs to be done.

status.description:
Current business status of the todo item.

Represents a normalized status code such as "ACTIVE" or "COMPLETED" that is backed by the `todo_app_todo_statuses` catalogue in the database.

Clients should treat this as an opaque status string and may combine it with `statusInfo` for display and advanced behaviour.

statusInfo.description:
Summary view of the status catalogue entry associated with this todo.

Provides additional metadata such as human-readable label, visual hints, and ordering information for the status referenced by the todo's underlying `todo_status_id` column. This association is read-only and derived from the todo's status foreign key.

Using this summary object avoids additional API calls when rendering todo lists that need both status codes and display-friendly status information.

due_date.description:
Optional due date and time by which the user aims to complete the todo.

This property maps to the nullable `due_date` column on the `todo_app_todos` table. When present, it is expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC and can be used by clients to sort, filter, or visually emphasize upcoming or overdue tasks.

If the underlying database value is null, this property may be omitted or explicitly set to null in the response depending on the API's null-handling conventions.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the todo item was initially created.

Expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC. This field is system-managed and read-only for clients.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to the todo item.

Expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC. This field is automatically maintained by the backend whenever mutable fields of the todo change.

completed_at.description:
Optional timestamp indicating when the todo entered a completed state.

This corresponds to the nullable `completed_at` column on the `todo_app_todos` table. When present, it records the moment the todo transitioned from an active state to a completed one and is expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC.

Clients can use this value to display completion information in history views or to sort completed tasks by their finish time.

ITodoAppTodoAdminAudit.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an administrative audit entry for a todo item within the todoApp service.

Used in list endpoints or embedded contexts where a lightweight view of admin actions on todos is required without full diff details or payload snapshots.

This summary embeds lightweight references to both the affected todo item and the acting administrator so that clients can immediately render meaningful context without additional lookup calls.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the admin audit record.

Generated by the system when the audit entry is created and never changes afterwards.

action.description:
Short machine-readable code describing what kind of administrative action was performed on the todo.

Typical example values include codes such as "update_status", "force_delete", or "restore". Clients should treat this as an opaque action code and use documentation or separate metadata to translate it into human-readable text.

field_name.description:
Optional name of the specific field on the todo that was affected by this administrative action.

This corresponds to the `field_name` column on the `todo_app_todo_admin_audits` table and is populated when an action targets a single attribute such as the title, description, or status. It is null for actions that are not tied to a single field, such as bulk status changes or deletions.

Consumers can use this value to render concise change summaries (for example, "status changed" or "title updated") without parsing the full before/after payloads.

previous_value.description:
Optional textual representation of the previous value of the affected field before the administrative change.

This maps to the `previous_value` column on `todo_app_todo_admin_audits` and is typically stored as a stringified snapshot that is meaningful to human operators (for example, the old title text or previous status code).

The field may be null for actions that do not have a clear "before" state, such as the initial creation of certain attributes or actions that act purely as flags.

new_value.description:
Optional textual representation of the new value of the affected field after the administrative change.

This corresponds to the `new_value` column in the `todo_app_todo_admin_audits` table and is used to reconstruct what state the administrator set as the result of the action, such as a new title, description, or status code.

The field may be null for deletions or for actions that conceptually clear a value rather than assigning a new one.

reason.description:
Optional free-form explanation recorded by the administrator to justify or provide context for the action.

This comes from the `reason` column on `todo_app_todo_admin_audits` and may describe policy considerations, abuse reports, user support tickets, or other business rationale for the change.

Downstream tools and reviewers can use this text when investigating unusual changes, handling appeals, or auditing compliance with internal procedures.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the administrative action was recorded.

Expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC. This is system-managed and read-only for clients.

todo.description:
Summary information about the Todo item that was affected by the administrative action.

Replaces the raw `todo_id` foreign key so that consumers can directly access key fields such as the todo identifier, title, and current status when displaying audit logs, without issuing additional lookup requests.

admin.description:
Summary information about the administrative user who performed the action on the todo item.

Replaces the raw `todo_app_todoadmin_id` foreign key and provides immediate access to identifying information about the acting administrator for traceability and audit list rendering.
